title: Work IQ: agents can execute reusable recipes
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the briefing presents general Work IQ permission, policy and billing controls as confirmed controls for recipes, although recipe-specific documentation was not found. It also incorrectly says the roadmap gives no cloud scope and omits the documented Microsoft Graph method for administering app consent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model for recipes is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" "licensing" "default". Opened Work IQ api-overview, enable-work-iq and retrieve and read cost-considerations search excerpts; they document general API billing, not recipe licensing.

claims.claim: Work IQ retrieve requires a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.
claims.quote: For `retrieve`, also complete the retrieve prerequisites, including Copilot Credits billing and a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Work IQ uses delegated Microsoft Entra authentication.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses Microsoft Entra ID delegated authentication.

claims.claim: Work IQ does not support application-only authentication.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.claim: Recipes use supported tools with the signed-in user's permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" "policy" "API". Opened api-overview, permissions and policy-governance-mcp; these establish user-scoped API access but do not describe recipe execution or its identity model.
claims.fix: Replace with 'General Work IQ API requests run in the context of the signed-in user; Microsoft has not documented the identity model or exact data reach for recipes.' Cite the API overview only for the general statement.

claims.claim: No separate admin-centre UI setting is documented for provisioning the Work IQ API service principal.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "enable" "Entra admin center" service principal. Opened enable-work-iq and Foundry work-iq; the browser-based provisioning procedure runs the Graph POST in Graph Explorer, not a separate admin-centre setting.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 provisions Work IQ for the organisation.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals. ... { "appId": "fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7" }

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table: grant consent
claims.claim: Granting consent follows Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > WorkIQAgent.Ask > Grant admin consent.
claims.quote: Grant consent: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Entra ID > App registrations > select the app > API permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant].
claims.fix: Separate the grant and revoke instructions. For grant use 'Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > Grant admin consent for [your tenant]'; do not insert WorkIQAgent.Ask as an intermediate grant step. Point docs to #admin-management.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table: revoke consent
claims.claim: Revoking consent uses the app's API permissions page, selects WorkIQAgent.Ask and then Revoke admin consent.
claims.quote: On the same API permissions page, select the WorkIQAgent.Ask permission and select Revoke admin consent.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for administering app consent is not documented.
claims.quote: You can use Microsoft Graph to grant or revoke API permissions for an app. ... The consentType is AllPrincipals, indicating that you're consenting on behalf of all users in the tenant.
claims.fix: Document POST /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants with clientId set to the client service-principal object ID, consentType AllPrincipals, resourceId set to the tenant's Work IQ service-principal object ID, and scope WorkIQAgent.Ask. For revocation document DELETE /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants/{grant-id}; warn that deleting a grant revokes all scopes in that grant. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-grant-via-msgraph and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/oauth2permissiongrant-post?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: Tenant-wide Work IQ MCP policy settings are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for configuring the tenant's Work IQ MCP policy is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy API configure settings; "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "PATCH". Opened policy-governance-mcp and read MCP overview, entity-model and tool-reference excerpts; no configuration endpoint or command was specified.

claims.claim: No recipe-specific control is documented on either the admin UI or API surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" controls enable default licensing authoring limits audit; "Work IQ" "recipes" "policy" "API". Opened enable-work-iq, permissions, policy-governance-mcp and Foundry work-iq; no recipe-specific control was stated.

claims.claim: Work IQ enablement, per-app consent and MCP policy are confirmed governance levers for recipes.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" "policy" "API". Opened api-overview, enable-work-iq, permissions and policy-governance-mcp; the latter focuses on MCP tool requests and none places recipes on that control surface.
claims.fix: Replace the opening governance paragraph with 'These are general Work IQ controls. Microsoft has not confirmed how they apply to recipes.' Put that qualification in the control notes and remove the assertion that recipes run inside this documented permission model.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy blocks mutation operations by default unless an administrator enables supported scenarios.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. ... Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center
claims.fix: Keep this scoped to the cited MCP policy documentation and note that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq#work-iq-key-features separately says 'Write operations are on by default' for the Microsoft Copilot harness experience. Do not promise either default for recipes.

claims.where: Governance controls: Credit consumption follows the tenant's spending policies
claims.claim: Recipe credit consumption follows the tenant's Copilot Credits spending policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" "licensing" "default"; "Work IQ" "retrieve" "spending policy". Opened Copilot Credits billing setup, api-overview and retrieve; none establishes recipe billing or spending-policy coverage.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Work IQ API usage has Copilot Credits spending controls; Microsoft has not published how recipe usage is charged or which spending policies cover it.' Retain the billing setup link only as general background.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating is justified despite recipe metering being unknown.
claims.quote: cost: "variable"; 'whether recipes follow the same model is unknown.' Standard: 'If licensing is not yet published, rate the cost that is known (low when the only cost the sources show is admin time)'.
claims.fix: Set cost to low and change its rationale to 'Low. Planning and review take administrator time; recipe licensing and metering are not yet published.' Do not use another Work IQ capability's meter to assign a factual recipe cost field.

claims.claim: Administrators can review audit logs for recipe runs.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "recipes" "audit logs". Read Work IQ overview's general tool-invocation logging statement and opened api-overview, policy-governance-mcp and Foundry work-iq; no accessible recipe-run audit log was documented.
claims.fix: Replace 'Review audit logs for recipe runs' with 'Before expanding a pilot, confirm which recipe execution records Microsoft exposes and how administrators can review them.' Keep recipe auditing as an open question.

claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the governance checklist asks administrators to use.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Agree an approval route for recipe authoring'; 'Limit recipe availability to a pilot'; 'Require human approval for write actions where supported'; 'Review audit logs for recipe runs'. Table: 'Control specific to recipes'.
claims.fix: Replace the catch-all recipe-control row with explicit rows for recipe authoring approval, pilot availability, human approval for writes and recipe-run monitoring, leaving both surfaces null where undocumented; alternatively rewrite these checklist items as decisions to investigate, not available configuration controls.
